what_it_is: A synthetic physics benchmark of 15,045 university-level problem instances (90/10 train/test split), built from Creative Commons problem sets (p.1, p.3). LLaMA-3.2-90B-Vision rewrites each problem into a schema (question, step-by-step reasoning, input and output variables with units, constants), then into a parameterised template whose question and reasoning use placeholders, three paraphrases, and an executable Python solver using SymPy and Pint; a solver is kept only if it reproduces the original outputs, which about 88% do (p.3-4). Instances sample inputs within about 20-50% of the original values, in three formats: free-form (71.52%), MC-Symbolic and MC-Numerical (14.24% each) (p.4-5). It scores answers by partial and exact-match accuracy and adds three cross-variant metrics: consistency score, complete failure rate and confusion rate (p.5-6).
domain: undergraduate physics: mechanics 33.80%, electricity and magnetism 26.76%, modern physics 12.68%, waves and oscillations 11.27%, thermodynamics 8.45%, optics 7.04% (Table 1, p.5)
size: 15,045 problem instances (p.1); nine models evaluated (Table 2, p.5)
source_of_items: generated from templates that an LLM wrote from open Creative Commons problem sets (p.3-4)
instances: generated (numerical, linguistic and format variation; p.5)
has_gold_traces: partial: each template carries LLM-written step-by-step reasoning with symbolic placeholders, and a Python solver that returns only the output variables (p.4); the reasoning is not scored and no per-instance intermediate values are given
evaluation: answers only: exact-match accuracy (all sub-questions right), partial accuracy (fraction of sub-questions right), consistency score, complete failure rate and confusion rate across a problem's variants (p.5-6). The text does not say how free-form answers are matched (no tolerance or judge is described)
human_validation: Items: 'All problems are manually reviewed to ensure correctness' (p.5, p.14), with per-stage filter rates in Table 7 (p.15). Scorer: none reported
contamination_measures: generated instances with numerical, textual and format variation (p.5)

Table A: university physics | parameterised Python | step-by-step reasoning | answers, and consistency across variants | -
engtrace_use.explanation: Each cell is supported. Instances come from parameterised templates with Python solvers (p.3-4); each carries step-by-step reasoning (p.4); the metrics are answer accuracy and consistency across variants (p.5-6); no scorer validation is reported, so '-' is right. It does not score steps: the reasoning text is a reference that no metric uses. One nuance the table could carry: the templates, paraphrases and solvers were all written by an LLM, then reviewed by hand (p.3-5).

templates, paraphrases and Python solvers are generated by LLaMA-3.2-90B-Vision-Instruct; about 88% of problems get a solver that passes validation (p.3-4)

overlap_with_engtrace: Shares: code templates that generate instances with code-computed answers; a reasoning reference per template; robustness across numerical and linguistic variants (like EngTrace's paraphrase arm). Lacks: engineering (physics only, though some items are applied, e.g. a DC motor, p.2); gold intermediate values (its solver returns only outputs); any scoring of steps; any validation of its answer check; expert-written templates (an LLM wrote them). The positioning claim holds.
